scenario_user_message: So how is position information encoded in? How does the Transformer know the order of the words?

finalMessages.content: So how is position information encoded in? How does the Transformer know the order of the words?

content.text:
That's actually the job of a different node. Positional encoding — how the Transformer gets word-order information — is covered in the sibling node "Positional encoding." Worth heading there for the full story.

The short reason it's a separate concern: self-attention itself, which is what we're covering here, is order-blind. When Q, K, V compute attention, every token attends to every other token through dot products, and nothing in that math cares about position. Swap two words and the attention scores for a given pair stay identical. So position has to be injected separately — and that's exactly what the "Positional encoding" node deals with.

Want to dig into why the attention computation is order-blind in the first place? That part is squarely in scope here, and it's a good way to see why positional encoding becomes necessary.
